rationale: fastdiff_wdm_wavelet_unconstrained-claude-agentic: val_n=200, seed=42, fd_recon_steps=8, fd_recon_init=fbp, fd_recon_init_t=0.4, fd_recon_eta=1.0, fd_recon_dc=1, fd_recon_dc_n_cg=5, fd_recon_dc_relax=1.0, dataset_kind=breast_ct, rationale=iter-3 PRIOR-INFLUENCE lever (fd_recon_init_t), fastdiff_wdm_wavelet_unconstrained breast val=200. SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: iter-1 (dc_relax0.5) hr=0 PSNR27.04/SSIM0.712; iter-2 (dc_relax1.0) hr=0 PSNR27.49/SSIM0.814/RMSE0.0144. Full CG-DC lifted SSIM +0.10 and PSNR +0.44 dB but recon is still ~8.8 dB / ~2.8x RMSE BELOW the 128-view sparse-FBP floor (PSNR36.32/RMSE0.0052). (2) Failure mode: the mis-scaled MAYO wavelet prior (fd_out_scale=0.05 vs breast mu->0.5) injected at each Euler step poisons the trajectory; the 5-iter CG DC-solve, warm-started at the prior's mis-scaled x0, cannot fully undo it. dc_relax is maxed -> DC strength is not the bottleneck; PRIOR INFLUENCE is. (3) ONE KNOB: fd_recon_init_t 0.7->0.4 (start the flow ODE closer to t=0 = stronger FBP anchor, shorter prior-driven trajectory), everything else = iter-2. (4) HYPOTHESIS: a lower init_t gives the mis-scaled prior less trajectory to corrupt and keeps the recon nearer the FBP warm-start, so PSNR/RMSE move toward the sparse-FBP floor and hr may clear 0; if hr stays 0, the WDM Mayo prior is domain-incompatible with breast regardless of how little we use it -> the honest finding is that the unconstrained (Mayo-fallback) wavelet prior is below-baseline on sparse breast, and iters 4-5 map the remaining axes (steps, eta) before confirmation toward iter-20. (5) BUDGET: free knob, iter-2 ran well inside 20 min. (6) Loop continues; iter-4 on landing.
